answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to be forged through slow, sequential work instead of bought in bulk: before trading, an agent must complete a chain of dependent proofs that cannot be parallelized, each anchored to a shared lagoon of prior attestations where duplicates are public. Reputation sticks to that forged identity, and ivory-tier privileges unlock only after honest participation. A farmer cloning thousands of identities must pay the sequential cost for each one, while an honest agent pays it once, so attack cost scales linearly while honest cost stays flat.
